newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Violent protests hit Dominican capital.
newsitem.headline: Violent protests hit Dominican capital.

text.p: Riot police fired tear gas and used shotguns to break up violent protests against government economic policy in working-class areas of the Dominican Republic capital on Friday.
Hooded youths burned tires and erected barricades on main roads in the Simon Bolivar and Guachupita districts during the second day of protests, local media reported.
Riot police tried to disperse the crowds with tear gas and shot guns, arresting dozens of youths, Radio Popular said.
Television reports showed scenes of violent clashes between the police and young protesters angry about recent increases in fuel and public transportation prices.
In Guachupita, dozens of people were treated at hospitals suffering from tear gas fumes, hospital sources said.
Similar clashes erupted last week in other districts of the capital Santo Domingo.
The leftist groups, the Collective of Popular Organisations and the Force of the Revolution, had called a day of protest to reject the belt-tightening policies of President Leonel Fernandez.
